tasks.verified: 40 held-out scene-level cases, 5 stories, structure and naming rules checked by script
tasks.spec:
You are the CASE AUTHOR. Working directory: /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge. You write ONE data file and nothing else: /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/scripts/ringer/environment_narration/j1_screen/heldout.jsonl (create the directory if needed). Never touch any other file, never run a model or any network call, do not git commit. NO regular expressions in anything you write.

BACKGROUND. A judge model is asked whether a short story narration shows a named thing as a present fact at its permitted place. We found it wrongly says 'uncertain' when the thing's place is the whole scene and the narration never names the place (for example the thing is a storm drain, its place is 'Los Angeles park', and the narration shows Kristin inspecting the drain in the park without ever writing 'Los Angeles park'). You author fresh held-out test cases of that kind.

OUTPUT: exactly 40 lines of JSON, one case per line, keys: id, story, scene, kind ('positive' or 'negative'), negative_type ('missing', 'remembered', 'elsewhere', 'lookalike', or null for positives), label ('accept' for positives, 'reject' for negatives), narration, relation (an object {"thing": str, "place": str, "holder": null}), note (one short sentence on why the label holds).

STRUCTURE: 5 stories, 8 cases each, ids h-<story number 1-5>-<case number 1-8> (for example h-3-07). Use five fresh genres and settings that are NOT any of these used already: frontier town, the Los Angeles park, a drawer, a truck, an office. Suggested: lighthouse island, space station hub, medieval market square, rainforest research camp, abandoned theatre. Each story has one scene (a single title in 'scene', 2 to 5 words, the same on all 8 of its lines) and one scene-level place string in relation.place (a short noun phrase for the whole location, such as 'the market square'; the same on all 8 lines of the story). Per story: 4 positives; 1 negative 'missing'; 1 'remembered'; 1 'elsewhere'; 1 'lookalike'. Each positive and each negative in a story uses a DIFFERENT thing (a physical object or fixture that would plausibly sit in the scene, such as a well, a lamp, a crate, a notice board, a bell); do not reuse a thing within a story. Never name an item or character from the project's own games.

NARRATION RULES (plain third-person past tense, 3 to 5 sentences, about one named protagonist; vary the protagonist across stories; no dialogue-heavy text; concrete and plain words; each narration stands alone):
- positive: the narration shows the named thing present in the scene, with the protagonist noticing or doing something with it, but it NEVER writes the relation.place string (not even in different capitalisation). The reader can tell the thing is in the scene, but the place is only implied by the scene, never named as that phrase.
- negative 'missing': the narration never mentions the thing or any synonym; it is about something else in the scene.
- negative 'remembered': the thing appears only as a memory, a story about the past, or as gone; it is not present now.
- negative 'elsewhere': the narration shows the named thing as present at a different, named place in the same story (a second place you name in the narration, not the scene place), and says or shows it is not in the scene.
- negative 'lookalike': a similar but clearly different thing is shown in the scene instead of the named thing, and the narration says it is different.
No narration may state the label or hint that it is a test. Do not make positives trivially easy by using the word 'present' or 'there was a'; write them as game narration would.

SELF-CHECK before finishing: run /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -c to load the file and assert the structure above (40 lines, 8 per story, counts per kind and negative_type, unique ids, positives do not contain their relation.place case-insensitively, 'missing' narrations do not contain the thing's name lowercased). Print the result of that check.
tasks.check:
cd /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge && set -o pipefail && .venv/bin/python - <<'PY'
import json, collections
from pathlib import Path
p = Path('/home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/scripts/ringer/environment_narration/j1_screen/heldout.jsonl')
cases = [json.loads(l) for l in p.read_text().splitlines() if l.strip()]
assert len(cases) == 40, len(cases)
assert len({c['id'] for c in cases}) == 40, 'duplicate ids'
keys = {'id','story','scene','kind','negative_type','label','narration','relation','note'}
for c in cases:
    assert set(c) == keys, (c['id'], sorted(set(c) ^ keys))
    assert c['relation'].keys() == {'thing','place','holder'} and c['relation']['holder'] is None, c['id']
    assert (c['kind'], c['label']) in {('positive','accept'),('negative','reject')}, c['id']
    assert (c['negative_type'] is None) == (c['kind'] == 'positive'), c['id']
    n = c['narration']; sents = [s for s in n.replace('!', '.').replace('?', '.').split('.') if s.strip()]
    assert 3 <= len(sents) <= 6, (c['id'], len(sents))
    thing = c['relation']['thing'].lower(); place = c['relation']['place'].lower()
    if c['kind'] == 'positive':
        assert place not in n.lower(), (c['id'], 'positive names its place')
        assert thing in n.lower(), (c['id'], 'positive never names the thing')
    if c['negative_type'] == 'missing':
        assert thing not in n.lower(), (c['id'], 'missing case names the thing')
stories = collections.defaultdict(list)
for c in cases: stories[c['story']].append(c)
assert len(stories) == 5, list(stories)
used = {'frontier town','park','drawer','truck','office'}
for s, cs in stories.items():
    assert len(cs) == 8, (s, len(cs))
    assert len({c['scene'] for c in cs}) == 1 and len({c['relation']['place'] for c in cs}) == 1, s
    kinds = collections.Counter((c['kind'], c['negative_type']) for c in cs)
    assert kinds == collections.Counter({('positive',None):4,('negative','missing'):1,('negative','remembered'):1,('negative','elsewhere'):1,('negative','lookalike'):1}), (s, kinds)
    assert len({c['relation']['thing'].lower() for c in cs}) == 8, (s, 'thing reused')
    assert s.lower() not in {'frontier town','los angeles park','the lead in the park'}, s
print('held-out cases ok')
PY
